terms.gloss: most, most people, the greater number
terms.grammar: adjective, plural (the singular plērusque is rare and post-classical)
evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.65: multī nihil prōdesse philosophiam, plērīque etiam obesse arbitrantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: It agrees with its noun, plērīque Belgae (Caes. BG 2.4), or takes ex (Lewis & Short). Often no stronger than “very many”.

terms.grammar: noun phrase, with a genitive of the whole
evidence: Sen. Ep. 1.1: magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus
terms.comment: Most of one thing: maxima pars vītae, most of one’s life.

terms.gloss: mostly, for the most part, usually
evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam
Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī

phrases.latin: plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent
phrases.english: most of the words we use every day, we don’t clearly know what they properly and truly mean

phrases.latin: quod plēraque nōs illā quasi mūgiente M litterā clūdimus
phrases.english: because we end most words with that letter M, which sounds almost like mooing

phrases.latin: eam plērīque scrīptōrēs, maximē quī sunt ab Isocrate, volunt esse lūcidam, brevem, vērīsimilem
phrases.english: most writers, especially those of Isocrates’ school, want it to be clear, short and believable

phrases.latin: magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus
phrases.english: a great part of life slips away while we do wrong, most of it while we do nothing, the whole of it while we do something else

phrases.latin: ōlim tōnsōrēs nōn fuisse adsignificant antīquōrum statuae, quod plēraeque habent capillum et barbam magnam
phrases.english: the old statues show that there were once no barbers, since most of them have long hair and a big beard

phrases.latin: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō
phrases.english: I wake when I please, mostly about sunrise, often before, seldom later

sources: Lewis & Short: plerique · Lewis & Short: magnus (maximus) · Lewis & Short: pars · Lewis & Short: plerumque
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-quintilianus, loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-varro, loci-plinius, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
